greater_aegis_of_athena.name: Greater Aegis of Athena
greater_aegis_of_athena.unidentified_name: a bright tasseled shield with a snake-haired face at its center
greater_aegis_of_athena.lore: Athena shook the aegis over armies to break their courage, and it was no ordinary shield, as Homer tells, but a goatskin hung with a hundred golden tassels and ringed about with Rout and Strife and Terror. After Perseus cut off the Gorgon's head he gave it to the goddess, and she fixed it at the center, so that the aegis carries the one face on which none could look and live. Whoever bears it has little to fear from a stony stare, and any foe that strikes at it may be given such a stare in return.

pridwen.name: Pridwen
pridwen.unidentified_name: a white round shield with a figure painted on the inside
pridwen.lore: When Arthur armed for the battle of Badon, as Geoffrey of Monmouth tells, he took the lance Ron, the sword Caliburn and a round shield called Pridwen, on whose inner face was painted the Virgin Mary, that the king might have her before his eyes whenever he raised his guard. The older poets of Wales give the same name to the ship in which he sailed into the Otherworld, so that by either telling it was Pridwen that carried him. The painted side is turned toward the bearer, and upon the other side spells are broken.

tower_shield_of_ajax.name: Tower Shield of Ajax
tower_shield_of_ajax.unidentified_name: a massive laminated shield of ox-hide and bronze
tower_shield_of_ajax.lore: Ajax carried a shield like a wall, which Tychius, the best leather cutter in Hyle, had made from seven layers of bull's hide with an eighth of bronze hammered over them, and when Hector's spear struck, it went through six hides and stopped in the seventh. Homer tells how the Trojans reached the ships and Ajax stood alone on the decks and held them off with a pike. Achilles had the greater brilliance, but it was Ajax whom none could move, and his shield is as immovable as he.

scutum_of_aeneas.name: Scutum of Aeneas
scutum_of_aeneas.unidentified_name: a curved rectangular shield of divine workmanship
scutum_of_aeneas.lore: At the asking of Venus her husband Vulcan forged arms for her son, and upon the shield, to which Virgil gave most of a book, the god hammered things that were yet to be: the she-wolf nursing the twins, the geese that saved the Capitol, the sea fight at Actium and Augustus in triumph. Aeneas admired the pictures, though he understood not one, and lifted onto his shoulder the fame and fortunes of all his descendants. It turns a sword for its bearer as surely as it foretold the days to come.

bronze_aegis.name: Bronze Aegis
bronze_aegis.unidentified_name: an ancient bronze shield, green with age
bronze_aegis.lore: Hephaestus the smith god made guardians of bronze and set them to their labours. The most famous was Talos, who walked the shore of Crete three times a day and threw boulders at strange ships, and through him from neck to ankle ran one vein, stopped with a single nail. The eye of the god is engraved upon this, the shield of such a bronze giant, and its curved face sheds a crushing blow better than any iron of its age.

aegis_of_athena.name: Aegis of Athena
aegis_of_athena.lore: For one purpose Athena lent Perseus her own shield, which was polished until it showed a face as clearly as still water. He walked backward toward the sleeping Gorgon, watching her in the bronze, and never once looked at her directly while he swung. The shield has kept its brightness ever since, and down in these depths a Gorgon who meets her own eyes in it fares no better than did her victims.
aegis_of_athena.special: A gaze meant for you freezes the one who looked.

lionheart_shield.name: Lionheart Shield
lionheart_shield.unidentified_name: a battered steel shield engraved with a lion
lionheart_shield.lore: Four months ago a knight carried this steel shield down into the dungeon, having promised his wife that he would be back for supper. A roaring lion is engraved upon it with the motto DUTY UNTO DEATH, and on the inside rim is inscribed the name MARTEN OF THE IRON VALE.

shield_of_the_spartans.name: Shield of the Spartans
shield_of_the_spartans.unidentified_name: a heavy round bronze shield painted with a red lambda
shield_of_the_spartans.lore: The mothers of Sparta, when they handed their sons this round shield, would say, as Plutarch records: come back with this, or on it. It was three feet of wood faced with bronze and marked with the lambda of Lacedaemon. An exiled king explained that a man wears helmet and breastplate for his own sake but carries the shield for the sake of the whole line, since its left half covers the soldier beside him, and for that reason to drop it was the one fault that was never forgiven.

svalinn.name: Svalinn
svalinn.unidentified_name: a golden shield that radiates warmth
svalinn.lore: In the Sayings of Grimnir it is sung how the horses Arvak and Alsvid drag the sun across the sky, and how Svalinn, the Cooling One, stands between her and the world, for if ever it fell from its place the mountains and the sea would burn. A shield that has shaded the earth from the sun itself is little troubled by a dragon, and when fire is hurled against it the flame is spent there, and some of it returns by the way it came.
svalinn.special: No fire can hurt you behind it.

ancile.name: Ancile
ancile.unidentified_name: an oval bronze shield with an angular notch
ancile.lore: While Numa Pompilius, the second king, reigned in Rome, a shield of bronze fell out of the sky, and a voice said that the city would rule for as long as the shield was kept. Numa therefore had the smith Mamurius Veturius make eleven copies so exact that no thief could pick out the true one, and the twelve hung in the house of Mars and were carried through the streets every March by the leaping priests. This is one of those twelve, and the arm that bears it grows strangely unhurried.

mycenaean_tower_of_telamon.name: Mycenaean Tower of Telamon
mycenaean_tower_of_telamon.lore: Telamon, the father of Ajax, bore a tower like his son's famous one when he went with Heracles to the first sack of Troy. It was made of eight layers of ox-hide stitched to a wicker frame and weighed more than its bearer's torso, for a Mycenaean fighter walked behind a shield as tall as himself, peering over the rim, and his body learned to lean into that weight as a sailor leans into a mast.

pelte_of_the_thracian.name: Pelte of the Thracian
pelte_of_the_thracian.lore: The peltasts of Thrace fought without armor, bearing only this crescent shield of wicker and goat-hide, and they skirmished, threw javelins and ran when the line came on, for such a shield was light enough to carry off in flight. The Greek hoplites scorned them as cowards, until the Athenian Iphicrates trained such peltasts, who broke a Spartan regiment with no heavier shield than this.

buckler_of_the_sumerian_lugal.name: Buckler of the Sumerian Lugal
buckler_of_the_sumerian_lugal.unidentified_name: a small round shield with cuneiform stamps
buckler_of_the_sumerian_lugal.lore: King Eannatum of Lagash beat the neighboring city of Umma around 2450 BC in a quarrel over a field, and had his victory carved upon the Stele of the Vultures, the oldest picture of a shield-wall that survives. There his spearmen march in a block over the fallen with shields locked rim to rim, while vultures carry off the heads. Such a king was called Lugal, which in Sumerian means big man, and the wedge marks stamped around the rim of this buckler give praise to Ningirsu, the god of Lagash.

khopesh_breaker_of_thebes.name: Khopesh-Breaker of Thebes
khopesh_breaker_of_thebes.unidentified_name: a tall Egyptian shield of cowhide and cedar
khopesh_breaker_of_thebes.lore: Mesehti, a governor in Egypt, took forty wooden model spearmen to his tomb at Asyut, and each of them holds a shield with a different pattern of hide. The foot soldiers of that land carried shields shaped like gravestones, flat at the bottom and rounded at the top, of cowhide with the hair left on, stretched over a wooden frame, both light and tall enough to crouch behind. When the sickle sword of that age, the khopesh, was swung at such a shield, it slid along the edge and found nothing to hook.

hittite_chariot_guard.name: Hittite Chariot-Guard
hittite_chariot_guard.unidentified_name: a waisted shield of dark hide, narrow in the middle
hittite_chariot_guard.lore: When the Hittites rode to war their heavier chariots carried three men where those of Egypt carried two, and beside the driver and the spearman stood a third whose only task was to hold a shield over both. At Kadesh in 1274 BC some twenty-five hundred of these chariots forded the Orontes and broke into the marching column of Ramesses II. Each king claimed the victory, and fifteen years later they signed the oldest peace between two great powers whose words survive. The shield is pinched at the waist so that a spear arm can work past it.

assyrian_siege_pavise.name: Assyrian Siege-Pavise
assyrian_siege_pavise.unidentified_name: a tall wickerwork shield with iron strips
assyrian_siege_pavise.lore: Sennacherib of Assyria took the Judean city of Lachish in 701 BC, and he was so proud of the deed that he had it carved about the walls of a chamber in his palace at Nineveh. In those carvings, which rest now in the British Museum, his archers go to war in pairs, and while one draws the bow his fellow plants before them a wicker screen taller than both, curved back at the top to catch the stones dropped from the wall. Such a screen is this, and though it is slow to shift it is very hard to shoot around.

spartan_aspis_of_leonidas.name: Spartan Aspis of Leonidas
spartan_aspis_of_leonidas.unidentified_name: a heavy bronze hoplon with a lambda chased in gold
spartan_aspis_of_leonidas.lore: King Leonidas of Sparta bore this shield, with its lambda chased in gold, when he led three hundred Spartans to Thermopylae, every one a father of living sons, and beside them stood seven hundred men of Thespiae who chose to stay to the end. A man of that country warned them that the arrows of the Persians would blot out the sun, and Herodotus tells that a Spartan named Dienekes answered that it was so much the better, for then they would fight in the shade.

etruscan_round_shield.name: Etruscan Round Shield
etruscan_round_shield.unidentified_name: a bronze-faced round shield with a gorgon boss
etruscan_round_shield.lore: While Rome was yet a cluster of huts, the Etruscans were lords of Italy north of the Tiber, and from them the Romans had kings, the arch, the triumph, and the rods and axe that are carried before a magistrate. Scholars can sound out their writing and understand but little of it, yet their painted tombs show them still in heavy armour, fighting in the Greek manner behind round shields faced with bronze, and from Greece also came the Gorgon upon this boss. Rome learned the phalanx from the Etruscans, and afterward swallowed them utterly.

scutum_of_the_legio.name: Scutum of the Legio
scutum_of_the_legio.unidentified_name: a curved red rectangular shield with gold wings
scutum_of_the_legio.lore: For the Twelfth Legion, which was called Fulminata and bore the thunderbolt as its badge, a common craftsman built this shield. He glued three layers of thin strips with the grain crossed, covered them with hide and linen, bound the rim and set an iron boss over the grip, and he curved the whole to wrap a man's body. Locked overhead and on every side, such shields made the tortoise, in which the legions walked up to the walls of cities under a rain of missiles, and behind work like his an empire was won.

macedonian_aspis_of_philip.name: Macedonian Aspis of Philip
macedonian_aspis_of_philip.unidentified_name: a small concave shield with a sunburst
macedonian_aspis_of_philip.lore: When Philip II of Macedon armed his foot soldiers with the sarissa, a pike eighteen feet long that needed both hands, he made their shield a small bowl of bronze, hung by a strap from the neck and slipped over the left forearm so that the hand was free. Five rows of points then reached out before the foremost rank, and his son Alexander carried that hedge of spears as far as the Indus. The rays upon the face of this shield are the star of the Macedonian kings, and they throw a little fire back upon those who send it.

celtic_oval_shield.name: Celtic Oval Shield
celtic_oval_shield.unidentified_name: an oval wooden shield with a spiral boss
celtic_oval_shield.lore: The Gauls went to war behind long oval shields of painted wood, with whorls upon them and an iron boss over the grip. Caesar relates that when the Helvetii locked theirs together and came against him, the Roman javelins pierced two shields at a stroke and pinned them fast, and the soft iron shanks bent, so that the men could neither draw them out nor fight with so burdened an arm, and many cast their shields away. Such oak was little defence against the javelin, though against the edge of a sword it stands far better.

germanic_kriegsschild.name: Germanic Kriegsschild
germanic_kriegsschild.unidentified_name: a planked round shield with a fur-wrapped rim
germanic_kriegsschild.lore: Among the tribes of Germany, as Tacitus wrote, there was little iron, and each painted its shields in chosen colours. No shame among them was deeper than the loss of a shield, and the warrior who left his upon the field was barred from sacrifice and council. In AD 9 Arminius led three legions of Rome into the Teutoburg Forest and destroyed them in three days, and men say that Augustus beat his head against a door, crying for his legions back. These planks are of that northern pine, which takes little harm from the cold.

sarmatian_lamellar_targe.name: Sarmatian Lamellar Targe
sarmatian_lamellar_targe.unidentified_name: a small lacquered shield of overlapping scales
sarmatian_lamellar_targe.lore: The Sarmatians were horsemen of the steppe who clad rider and steed alike in overlapping scales, cut at times from horn or hoof when iron was scarce. Marcus Aurelius overcame them upon the frozen Danube and took eight thousand of their cavalry into the service of Rome, and of these he sent fifty-five hundred to Britain. There, as some scholars believe, their dragon banners and their tales of a sword set in the earth lingered until they had passed into the legend of Arthur.

battersea_votive_shield.name: Battersea Votive Shield
battersea_votive_shield.unidentified_name: a thin bronze shield set with red glass studs
battersea_votive_shield.lore: In the age of iron the Britons had a custom of giving to their gods the finest thing their smiths could make. So this facing of bronze was wrought in flowing curves and set with twenty-seven studs of red glass, too thin and too short to turn a spear, and was cast into the Thames for a god whose name is forgotten. There it lay until workmen dredged it up at Battersea in 1857, and a gift so given has still a claim upon the unseen powers, so that their sorceries fall more lightly on its bearer.

saxon_round_shield.name: Saxon Round Shield
saxon_round_shield.unidentified_name: a round limewood shield with gilded beast fittings
saxon_round_shield.lore: A great ship was buried at Sutton Hoo, and most scholars believe that the man who was laid in it was Raedwald, king of the East Angles, who died about 624. Beside him lay a shield of limewood covered with hide, with a heavy boss of iron and gilded shapes of a dragon and a bird of prey. The poets of his people called a shield simply 'the linden,' and in battle their warriors stood rim over rim in the shield wall. It was of such boards as this that the poet of Beowulf was thinking when he sang of war.

lendings_of_beowulf.name: Lendings of Beowulf
lendings_of_beowulf.unidentified_name: a round shield of solid iron, scorched blue at the rim
lendings_of_beowulf.lore: For fifty years Beowulf had ruled the Geats, until a thief stole a cup from a dragon's hoard and the dragon burned the king's hall. Knowing that linden would not endure such breath, the old king bade a shield be made all of iron, and he set out with eleven companions and the thief to show the way. Ten of them fled to the wood when the fire came, but young Wiglaf stayed, and when his own shield was burned he sheltered behind the king's. The iron held long enough for those two to slay the worm, and fire still does poorly against it.

sigurds_handshield.name: Sigurd's Handshield
sigurds_handshield.unidentified_name: a small gilt buckler painted with a coiled serpent
sigurds_handshield.lore: When Sigurd rode into the hall of King Gjuki, so says the saga of the Volsungs, his shield was overlaid with red gold and painted with a dragon, dark brown above and red beneath, and helm, saddle and surcoat bore the same device, that all who saw him might know him for the slayer of the great worm Fafnir. The tale is carved also upon the rock of Ramsund in Sweden. He put his trust in the sword Gram before any shield, and for that reason the one he carried was small.

carolingian_kite.name: Carolingian Kite
carolingian_kite.unidentified_name: an almond-shaped shield with a long lower point
carolingian_kite.lore: Merchants call this pattern Carolingian, though the riders of Charlemagne bore round shields and the long kite came two centuries after them. Beneath a round shield a horseman's left leg hangs bare, and so some forgotten maker drew the lower rim down to a point, that it might cover him from knee to ankle. The Bayeux Tapestry shows such shields on nearly every Norman arm at Hastings. Within a lifetime every knight from Sicily to Scotland rode behind one, and upon that long curve the point of a lance will skid aside.

heater_of_the_black_prince.name: Heater of the Black Prince
heater_of_the_black_prince.unidentified_name: a flat-topped black shield bearing three white feathers
heater_of_the_black_prince.lore: Edward of Woodstock, whom men called the Black Prince, led a wing at Crecy when he was sixteen years old, and his father would send him no help, saying that the boy should win his spurs. Ten years afterward at Poitiers he took the king of France captive. For the tourney he bore three white ostrich feathers on a black shield with the motto Ich dien, I serve, which the Princes of Wales bear still. But he died a year before his father and never wore the crown, and his shield, helm and gauntlets are kept beside his tomb at Canterbury.

mameluke_targe.name: Mameluke Targe
mameluke_targe.unidentified_name: a small round shield inlaid with golden arabesques
mameluke_targe.lore: Bought as boys upon the steppe and reared in the barracks of Cairo, the Mamluks spent long years in mastering bow, lance and saber, until in 1250 they took Egypt from their own masters. Ten years later, under Qutuz and Baybars, they gave a host of Mongols its first great defeat at Ain Jalut. When Napoleon broke their charge at the Pyramids in 1798 he so admired them that he took a squadron into his own guard. The small steel shields they bore, of which this is one, were made for saber work on horseback.

o_tate_of_the_samurai.name: O-Tate of the Samurai
o_tate_of_the_samurai.unidentified_name: a tall lacquered wooden screen on a single leg
o_tate_of_the_samurai.lore: The samurai had need of both hands, first for the bow and later for the sword, and so the warriors of Japan took no shield upon the arm. They set up instead the tate, a screen of planks as tall as a man with a prop hinged behind it, and made of these a wall from which archers and gunners fought. At Nagashino in 1575 Oda Nobunaga placed his guns behind stockade and screen, and the horsemen of the Takeda clan charged and never reached them. Arrows and shot that strike such planks thud into the wood and go no farther.

skidbladnir_aegis.name: Skidbladnir Aegis
skidbladnir_aegis.unidentified_name: a pale shield carved with miniature ship-figures
skidbladnir_aegis.lore: For the god Freyr the dwarf sons of Ivaldi built Skidbladnir, a ship so great that all the gods might board it fully armed, which had a fair wind as soon as the sail was raised and at the voyage's end could be folded like a cloth and put into his pouch. A lesser smith afterward carved its likeness upon this pale shield and caught a little of their craft, so that cold folds itself away before ever it reaches the bearer.

smoking_mirror_of_tezcatlipoca.name: Smoking Mirror of Tezcatlipoca
smoking_mirror_of_tezcatlipoca.unidentified_name: a round shield faced with polished black obsidian
smoking_mirror_of_tezcatlipoca.lore: Tezcatlipoca, whom the Aztecs held for the god of night and sorcery, carried a mirror of obsidian that showed the souls of all who looked into it. Quetzalcoatl beheld his own ugly face there and fled for shame, and from that hour began the long unravelling that ended in conquest. This shield has the virtue of that glass, for when an enemy hurls a spell against it the shield turns the spell about and shows the caster the very thing he meant to do.

vajra_paramita.name: Vajra Paramita
vajra_paramita.unidentified_name: a small round shield inscribed with a thunderbolt
vajra_paramita.lore: When the drought-serpent Vritra withheld the waters from the world, the sage Dadhichi gave up his life, as Hindu tradition tells, that the gods might make from his bones the vajra, which is both thunderbolt and diamond and breaks all things while nothing can break it, and with it Indra slew the serpent. In the vajra the Buddhists see the mind that nothing shatters, and they teach that six perfections, giving, discipline, patience, effort, meditation and wisdom, will carry a soul to the farther shore. This shield is marked with the signs of both.

horse_armor_of_the_norns.name: Horse-Armor of the Norns
horse_armor_of_the_norns.unidentified_name: a kite shield carved with three women at a well
horse_armor_of_the_norns.lore: Beside the well beneath the World Tree dwell Urd, Verdandi and Skuld, who are what was, what is becoming and what is owed. Each day they lay white clay and water from the well upon the roots lest the tree should rot. They cut also the fate of every child that is born, and the gods who hold court beside them cannot overrule them. The three are carved upon this shield, and they return whatever is sent against it, for they count a spell a debt like any other and require that it be repaid.

scarab_of_apophis_binding.name: Scarab of Apophis-Binding
scarab_of_apophis_binding.unidentified_name: a round shield carved as a green stone beetle
scarab_of_apophis_binding.lore: Each night Ra sails his boat through the underworld, and each night the serpent Apophis rises to swallow it and is speared by Set from the prow. In the world above, the priests of Karnak lent their aid by making a serpent of wax with the name written on it, which they spat upon, trampled and burned as they read from the Book of Overthrowing Apophis, until at dawn Khepri the scarab rolled the sun over the rim of the world. Their spells are cut upon this beetle of green stone, and by their virtue it turns malice back.

yamas_dharma_watch.name: Yama's Dharma-Watch
yamas_dharma_watch.unidentified_name: a black iron kite shield with a buffalo-horn crest
yamas_dharma_watch.lore: Yama was the first of mortals to die, as the oldest hymns of India relate, and because he found the road to the other world he was made its king. He rides upon a black buffalo with a noose in his hand for the drawing out of souls, and in Tibet he wears the buffalo's head himself and holds aloft the mirror of karma, wherein the dead behold every deed of their lives. From the rim of that mirror this shield was forged, so that whatever is aimed at its bearer is first weighed, and much is found wanting and turned away.

hrungnirs_stone_shield.name: Hrungnir's Stone Shield
hrungnirs_stone_shield.unidentified_name: a slab of grey stone with a grip cut into the back
hrungnirs_stone_shield.lore: Hrungnir, the strongest of the giants, came to his duel with Thor bearing this shield of stone, broad as a door. But Thjalfi, the servant of Thor, ran to him and said that he held it amiss, since his master meant to come at him from beneath the earth. The giant believed him and laid the shield flat and stood upon it, and Thor came from in front with the hammer. The shield was never at fault, and it will guard very well whoever holds it upright.

shield_of_achilles.name: Shield of Achilles
shield_of_achilles.unidentified_name: a great round shield worked with tiny figures, a river running round its rim
shield_of_achilles.lore: When Patroclus had fallen in the armour of Achilles, the sea-goddess Thetis went up to Olympus for her son's sake, and at her asking Hephaestus the smith made this shield in a single night. He wrought upon it earth, sea and sky, with the sun, the moon and the stars, two cities, one at a wedding and one under siege, men at the plough and at the reaping, and about the rim the river Ocean. Beneath these he laid five layers, two of bronze, two of tin and one of gold, and in the battles that followed the spear of Aeneas passed through two of them and was stayed by the gold, and the spear of Hector leapt back from its face.

shield_of_ilion.name: Shield of Ilion
shield_of_ilion.unidentified_name: an ancient round bronze shield, worn smooth and green with age
shield_of_ilion.lore: Alexander, when first he came into Asia, went up to Troy and sacrificed to Athena of Ilion, and he hung his own armour in her temple and took in its stead some of the sacred arms that had lain there since the Trojan War. From that day his shield-bearers carried this shield before him into battle. Long afterward in India he leapt down within the wall of a town of the Malli with but three men beside him, and an arrow passed through his breastplate into his chest. He fell, and Peucestas stood over him with the sacred shield of Troy until the Macedonians broke in, and so the king lived, as the historian Arrian has set down.

joans_standard.name: Joan of Arc's Standard
joans_standard.unidentified_name: a long white banner on a pole, sown with gold lilies
joans_standard.lore: At the bidding of her Voices, Joan of Arc had this standard made at Tours in 1429, of white sown with gold lilies, showing the Lord with the world in His hand and an angel on either side, and bearing the names Jhesus Maria. At Orléans she bade her soldiers watch it, and when its tail touched the wall of the English fort they went over and took the place. Afterward, when her judges asked whether she loved better her standard or her sword, she answered that she loved the standard forty times more, and that she bore it herself in the charge so that she might kill no one.
